amulung.description: municipality of the Philippines in the province of Cagayan

commons.description: The flag of Amulung, Cagayan, Philippines. On a white field, it reads "AMULUNG: THE LAND OF SMILING BEAUTY" in black text along the top. Below it, there is a large, yellow sun to the left. Three large, tapered, curved squiggles with two humps stretching from left to right, overlap the sun, so the sun appears only as a crescent with curved rays alongside the outside edge. The squiggles are, from top to bottom, green, blue, and green again, like a river between grass. There are six, small, simplified human figures that are colored red. Three of them are in the valley between the humps on the top, and the other three are under the right of the two arches formed by the squiggles.
commons.artist: DADDA NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL (Amulung, Cagayan, Philippines)

commons.description: Flag of Milford in Nebraska, created according to File:Flag of Milford, NE.png. It seems that the uploader is the flag's creator, Nolan Eickhoff, so it has been released as CC BY SA 4.0. Though, it seems that it meets the requirements for PD-shape. As FOTW notes, "According to Eickhoff, the white symbolizes peace, the black justice, the grey bravery, the purple kindness and the gold prosperity. The shape of the lines represents Milford moving forward, as it resembles an arrow pointing toward the future. The mill wheel is for the old mill that the town is named after, and the wheat is for the agriculture the town is based on."

commons.description:
Flag created by CincyFlags for the neighborhood. 
Its symbolism, according to CincyFlags in [1]:
"A stylized pin oak leaf representing the trees that were planted in the front yards of houses when the neighborhood was established.
A green hill for the old farmlands that used to make up the neighborhood. The curved, wave-like shape evokes the winding Miami & Erie canal that used to run along Tennessee Avenue.
A stylized “A” shape for the striking Tudor-style houses in Paddock Hills.
Orange, White and Yellow are warm colors taken from the old neighborhood sign.

Green for the vibrant nature and Avon Woods Preserve."
